hook: Was wäre, wenn deutsche Forscher einen Weg gefunden haben, Ihre körpereigene GLP-1-Produktion zu aktivieren? (What if German researchers found a way to activate your own GLP-1 production?)
claim: MetaboSana is a German-language metabolism and weight capsule that claims to activate the body's own GLP-1 production, positioning itself against weight-loss injections. It's part of the same '-Sana' product family as CleanseSana.
ing_note: MetaboSana publishes its doses per capsule: alpha-lipoic acid 75 mg, green tea EGCG 75 mg, berberine HCl 50 mg, chromium picolinate 50 mcg, banaba leaf 1 mg, zinc gluconate 5.5 mg, milk thistle 50 mg, resveratrol 20 mg, Korean ginseng 2.5 mg and cayenne 2.5 mg. Studies of berberine used 1,000–1,500 mg a day, 20–30 times more than one capsule provides.
use: One capsule a day, according to the page.
price_note: MetaboSana is sold in euro packages (1, 3 or 6 units) with lower per-bottle prices on larger packages; totals appear on the order page.
checks: No supplement has been shown to raise GLP-1 to anything like the levels produced by semaglutide or tirzepatide injections.
Berberine at 50 mg is far below studied doses, and banaba at 1 mg and ginseng at 2.5 mg are token amounts.
The page claims cayenne and EGCG give '340% stronger thermogenesis', which isn't a figure from human research.
Publishing doses is good practice, and it lets readers see how small they are.
cons: Most doses far below studied amounts
verdict: MetaboSana deserves credit for transparency, but the doses it publishes show it can't do what it promises. Anyone interested in GLP-1 medicines should discuss them with a doctor, and anyone wanting berberine should know that studied doses are much higher (and interact with diabetes medicine).
